claim: Fgd5 was identified as a HSC-expressed gene that is rapidly downregulated upon differentiation through a transcriptome based screen of more than 40 different hematopoietic cell types.
source: Using a transcriptome based screen of more than 40 different hematopoietic cell types, Fgd5 (FYVE, RhoGEF and PH domain containing 5) was identified as a HSC-expressed gene that is rapidly downregulated upon differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Gazit et al., 2014) that performed the transcriptome screen.

claim: Fgd5 expression marks all HSCs as confirmed through functional studies using an Fgd5 knock-in reporter strain.
source: That Fgd5 expression marks all HSCs was confirmed through functional studies using an Fgd5 knock-in reporter strain (Gazit et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gazit et al., 2014 which performed functional studies.

claim: Transcriptome data was acquired from 11,581 individual lineage-marker negative, c-kit positive and CD45 positive bone marrow cells (Lin-kit+).
source: To further detail the HSC specificity of Fgd5, we first acquired transcriptome data from 11,581 individual lineage-marker negative, c-kit positive and CD45 positive bone marrow cells (Lin-kit+).
evidence: The claim describes experimental data collection performed in this study.

claim: The Lin-kit+ population contains a range of different immature hematopoietic progenitor cells.
source: The Lin-kit+ population contains a range of different immature hematopoietic progenitor cells (Pronk et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Pronk et al., 2007.

claim: 793 Lin-kit+Fgd5+ cells were sorted and analyzed.
source: We sorted either Lin-kit+Fgd5+ cells (Figure 1A middle; 793 cells, Fgd5+)
evidence: The claim describes experimental data from cell sorting performed in this study.

claim: 519 Fgd5+ cells with a stringent Lin-kit+Sca-1+CD48-CD150+ HSC phenotype were sorted and analyzed.
source: or Fgd5+ cells with a stringent Lin-kit+Sca-1+CD48-CD150+ HSC phenotype (Figure 1A right, 519 cells, HSC-Fgd5+).
evidence: The claim describes experimental data from cell sorting performed in this study.

claim: Fgd5+ cells and HSC-Fgd5+ cells form a distinct and highly overlapping cluster in tSNE analysis.
source: Fgd5+ cells, regardless if sorted based on additional HSC markers, formed a distinct and highly overlapping cluster (Figure 1A, middle and right).
evidence: The claim is supported by data visualization in Figure 1A showing the clustering pattern.

claim: The Fgd5+ cell cluster localizes to a region with very few cells when evaluating Lin-kit+ cells, emphasizing the HSC-specificity of the Fgd5 reporter.
source: This cluster localized to a region with very few cells when evaluating Lin-kit+ cells (Figure 1A, left, dotted area), emphasizing the HSC-specificity of the Fgd5 reporter and the low HSC frequency within the larger Lin-kit+ fraction.
evidence: The claim is supported by data visualization in Figure 1A showing the spatial relationship of clusters.

claim: The Fgd5+ cell cluster demonstrates the low HSC frequency within the larger Lin-kit+ fraction.
source: This cluster localized to a region with very few cells when evaluating Lin-kit+ cells (Figure 1A, left, dotted area), emphasizing the HSC-specificity of the Fgd5 reporter and the low HSC frequency within the larger Lin-kit+ fraction.
evidence: The claim is supported by data visualization in Figure 1A showing the spatial relationship of clusters.

claim: Tamoxifen administration to Fgd5CreERT2/+; Rosa26lsl-Tomato/+ mice leads to irreversible and heritable Tomato labeling of HSCs and their offspring.
source: In this model, HSCs can be identified based on ZsGreen expression, while Tamoxifen administration leads to irreversible and heritable Tomato labeling of HSCs and, over time, their offspring (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental design and expected outcome of the lineage tracing model.

claim: 48 hours after a single injection of Tamoxifen, a fraction of candidate HSCs are labeled with Tomato, with virtually no labeling in other c-kit+ progenitor fractions.
source: To confirm the model, we evaluated Tomato label in HSC and BM progenitor cells 48 hr after a single injection (1x) of Tamoxifen. This revealed labeling of a fraction of candidate HSCs, with virtually no labeling in other c-kit+ progenitor fractions (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The labeling pattern establishes HSC specific labeling and a relatively low differentiation rate of HSCs in steady state.
source: This established HSC specific labeling and a relatively low differentiation rate of HSCs in steady state (Säwén et al., 2016; Wilson et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and citations to Säwén et al., 2016 and Wilson et al., 2008.

claim: Among HSCs, there is a strong correlation between a restricted proliferative history and Tomato labeling.
source: Among HSCs, this revealed a strong correlation between a restricted proliferative history and Tomato labeling.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from H2B-mCherry label retention analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: A single dose of Tamoxifen is insufficient to label all candidate Fgd5-expressing HSCs.
source: Of note, a single dose of Tamoxifen was insufficient to label all candidate Fgd5-expressing HSCs (Figure 1E and data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 5 out of 8 recipients transplanted with Tomato+ HSCs showed long-term multilineage reconstitution.
source: This revealed long-term multilineage reconstitution in 5/8 recipients transplanted with Tomato+ HSCs (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental transplantation data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The mean fraction of Tomato+ HSCs is 13% ± 9%.
source: The frequencies of Tomato+ cells for each investigated subset were next related to the fraction of Tomato labeled HSCs (Figure 2A, mean 13% ± 9%) in individual mice (Figure 2B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The fraction of labeled HSCs is generally higher in mice analyzed beyond 4 days of chase compared to mice analyzed after shorter chase periods.
source: The fraction of labeled HSCs was generally higher in mice analyzed beyond 4 days of chase compared to mice analyzed after shorter chase periods.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the time course analysis.

claim: No further increase in HSC labeling is noted after longer periods of chase beyond 4 days.
source: However, no further increase in HSC labeling was noted after longer periods of chase (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: LSKCD150-CD48- MPPs are immature multipotent progenitors distinguished from HSCs by their limited self-renewal potential.
source: LSKCD150-CD48- MPPs are immature multipotent progenitors distinguished from HSCs by their limited self-renewal potential (Kiel et al., 2005; Kiel et al., 2008; Ugale et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kiel et al., 2005, Kiel et al., 2008, and Ugale et al., 2014.

claim: LSKCD150-CD48- MPPs are generated from HSCs with the fastest kinetics among evaluated progenitor subsets, with near equilibrium to HSC label reached by 4 weeks.
source: Of the evaluated progenitor subsets in our work, this subset was generated from HSCs with the fastest kinetics, with near equilibrium to HSC label reached already by 4 weeks (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: MPP2 cells cluster closely to Meg/E progenitors in PCA analysis of gene expression data.
source: Visualization of this data using PCA revealed that MPP2 cells clustered closely to Meg/E progenitors (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data visualized in Figure 2C.

claim: Short-term (6 days) culture experiments reveal more robust generation of both megakaryocyte and erythroid containing colonies from MPP2s compared to other LSK subsets.
source: Consistent with a close association to the Meg/E lineages, short-term (6 days) culture experiments revealed a more robust generation of both megakaryocyte and erythroid containing colonies from MPP2s compared to other LSK subsets (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental culture data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: MPP2 cells reach label equilibrium with HSCs after 32 weeks in 1x injected mice.
source: When investigating Tomato label progression, MPP2 cells reached label equilibrium with HSCs after 32 weeks in 1x injected mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: MPP3/4 cells lack, for the most part, Meg/E lineage potential.
source: MPP3/4 cells lack, for the most part, Meg/E lineage potential (Adolfsson et al., 2005; Arinobu et al., 2007; Pietras et al., 2015; Pronk et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Adolfsson et al., 2005, Arinobu et al., 2007, Pietras et al., 2015, and Pronk et al., 2007.

claim: MPP3/4 cells acquire Tomato label with much slower kinetics compared to other LSK fractions.
source: MPP3/4 cells acquired Tomato label with much slower kinetics compared to other LSK fractions (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Megakaryocyte progenitors (MkP) acquire label with the fastest kinetics among distinct progenitor fractions within the Lin-kit+ fraction, reaching label equilibrium with HSCs after 32 weeks.
source: Of the distinct progenitor fractions within the Lin-kit+ fraction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), megakaryocyte progenitors (MkP) acquired label with the fastest kinetics, reaching label equilibrium with HSCs after 32 weeks.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Pre-megakaryocytic/erythroid (preMeg/E), pre-colony forming unit-erythroid (pre CFU-E) and pre-granulocyte-macrophage (preGM) progenitors acquire Tomato label with very similar kinetics despite their distinct lineage affiliations.
source: Other myeloerythroid progenitors, including pre-megakaryocytic/erythroid (preMeg/E), pre-colony forming unit-erythroid (pre CFU-E) and pre-granulocyte-macrophage (preGM) progenitors acquired Tomato label with very similar kinetics despite their distinct lineage affiliations, although they never quite reached an equilibrium with HSCs throughout the course of the experiments (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pre-megakaryocytic/erythroid (preMeg/E), pre-colony forming unit-erythroid (pre CFU-E) and pre-granulocyte-macrophage (preGM) progenitors never quite reach equilibrium with HSCs throughout the course of the experiments.
source: Other myeloerythroid progenitors, including pre-megakaryocytic/erythroid (preMeg/E), pre-colony forming unit-erythroid (pre CFU-E) and pre-granulocyte-macrophage (preGM) progenitors acquired Tomato label with very similar kinetics despite their distinct lineage affiliations, although they never quite reached an equilibrium with HSCs throughout the course of the experiments (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Myeloerythroid cells acquire label more rapidly than lymphoid cells.
source: First, we made the general observation that myeloerythroid cells acquired label more rapidly than lymphoid cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the lineage tracing experiments.

claim: Among myeloid subsets, platelets acquire Tomato label with the fastest kinetics, followed by granulocytes and erythrocytes.
source: Among the myeloid subsets, platelets acquired Tomato label with the fastest kinetics, followed by granulocytes and erythrocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Among lymphoid cell types, NK cells display faster labeling kinetics followed by B cells.
source: Among lymphoid cell types, NK cells displayed faster labeling kinetics followed by B cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: T cells show the slowest labeling kinetics among lymphoid cells.
source: T cells showed the slowest labeling kinetics among lymphoid cells and CD4+ T cells acquired label faster than CD8+ T cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CD4+ T cells acquire label faster than CD8+ T cells.
source: T cells showed the slowest labeling kinetics among lymphoid cells and CD4+ T cells acquired label faster than CD8+ T cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The frequency of Tomato+ cells increases over time in all evaluated lineages, demonstrating a continuous contribution of HSCs to all hematopoietic lineages.
source: Because the frequency of Tomato+ cells increased over time in all evaluated lineages, this data demonstrate a continuous contribution of HSCs to all hematopoietic lineages.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the time course analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: At the earliest time points evaluated, a higher label is observed in candidate committed myeloerythroid progenitors compared to their corresponding mature cell lineages.
source: At the earliest time points evaluated, we observed for all evaluated fractions a higher label in their corresponding progenitors (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The label ratio between progenitors and mature cells reaches similar equilibrium ratios for all evaluated lineages during the course of the experiments, although the erythroid lineage displays somewhat slower kinetics.
source: However, this was resolved during the course of the experiments and reached similar equilibrium ratios for all evaluated lineages, although the erythroid lineage displayed somewhat slower kinetics (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Previously proposed progenitors appear to be, at least for the most part, obligatory intermediates in hematopoiesis.
source: Collectively, these experiments are in line with the view that progenitor generation precedes the generation of mature cells and that previously proposed progenitors appears to be, at least for the most part, obligatory intermediates.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing the temporal relationship between progenitor and mature cell labeling.

claim: Hematopoiesis after transplantation of HSCs is fundamentally different from unperturbed hematopoiesis.
source: Hematopoiesis after transplantation of HSCs is fundamentally different from unperturbed hematopoiesis (Busch et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Busch et al., 2015 and Sun et al., 2014.

claim: Label progression in transplanted mice is faster compared to steady state.
source: Compared to steady state, label progression in transplanted mice were faster (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: HSC transplantation results in faster label progression compared to WBM transplantation, especially into the B cell lineage.
source: When label progression kinetics was compared between HSC and WBM transplanted animals, HSC transplantation resulted in faster label progression, especially into the B cell lineage (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The faster B cell label progression after HSC transplantation compared to WBM transplantation likely reflects a significant contribution to the regeneration of the B cell lineage by co-transplanted long-lived B-lineage progenitors and mature cells after WBM transplantation.
source: This likely reflects a significant contribution to the regeneration of the B cell lineage by co-transplanted long-lived B-lineage progenitors and mature cells after WBM transplantation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data comparing HSC and WBM transplantation.

claim: Label progression after WBM transplantation into irradiated or non-irradiated/antibody-mediated conditioned recipient mice reveals similar label progression kinetics into most mature lineages, with the exception of platelets that display faster label progression in irradiated mice.
source: Comparison of label progression after WBM transplantation into irradiated or non-irradiated/antibody-mediated conditioned recipient mice revealed similar label progression kinetics into most mature lineages, with the exception of platelets that displayed a faster label progression in irradiated mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Progenitors for platelets are more effectively ablated by irradiation than antibody-mediated pre-conditioning.
source: This suggests that progenitors for platelets are more effectively ablated by irradiation than antibody-mediated pre-conditioning.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data comparing different conditioning regimens.

claim: Prolonged Tamoxifen treatment does not induce any additional proliferation within the HSC compartment.
source: Prolonged Tamoxifen treatment did not induce any additional proliferation within the HSC compartment, while more differentiated progenitors had readily proliferated in both settings (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from H2B-mCherry label retention shown in Figure 3A.

claim: More differentiated progenitors readily proliferate in both Tamoxifen-treated and control settings.
source: Prolonged Tamoxifen treatment did not induce any additional proliferation within the HSC compartment, while more differentiated progenitors had readily proliferated in both settings (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from H2B-mCherry label retention shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A 16 week labeling period followed by a chase period results in labeling of virtually all candidate HSCs.
source: This labeling strategy resulted in labeling of virtually all candidate HSCs (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A more complete HSC labeling results in somewhat faster and more robust label progression into all PB cell subsets compared to 1x Tamoxifen labeling.
source: However, a more complete HSC labeling resulted in a somewhat faster and more robust label progression into all PB cell subsets compared to 1x Tamoxifen labeling (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing different labeling strategies shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The more complete HSC labeling effect is most evident for the lymphoid lineages, where the majority of PB cells have been generated from HSCs at the experiment end point upon prolonged Tamoxifen administration.
source: This was most evident for the lymphoid lineages, where the majority of PB cells had been generated from HSCs at the experiment end point upon prolonged Tamoxifen administration, whereas the ratio of labeled lymphocytes vs. labeled HSCs was low (>0,5) even after 83 weeks of chase in 1x Tamoxifen labeled mice (Figure 2B, Figure 2E and Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, Figure 2E and Figure 3B.

claim: Granulocytes in the skin epidermis are almost completely Tomato positive in mice with nearly complete HSC labeling.
source: Granulocytes were almost completely Tomato positive, while Langerhans cells were devoid of label (Figure 3D, lower left), in line with the fetal origin and self-maintenance of the latter cells (Collin and Milne, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Langerhans cells in the skin epidermis are devoid of Tomato label in mice with nearly complete HSC labeling.
source: Granulocytes were almost completely Tomato positive, while Langerhans cells were devoid of label (Figure 3D, lower left), in line with the fetal origin and self-maintenance of the latter cells (Collin and Milne, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and citation to Collin and Milne, 2016.

claim: Langerhans cells have a fetal origin and self-maintenance.
source: Granulocytes were almost completely Tomato positive, while Langerhans cells were devoid of label (Figure 3D, lower left), in line with the fetal origin and self-maintenance of the latter cells (Collin and Milne, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Collin and Milne, 2016.

claim: Vγ3δ+ T cells are an established fetal derived T cell subset.
source: Next, we interrogated Tomato expression in Vγ3δ+ T cells, an established fetal derived T cell subset (Havran and Allison, 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Havran and Allison, 1990.

claim: Vγ3δ+ T cells display robust Tomato labeling in the lineage tracing model.
source: To our surprise, this revealed robust Tomato labeling of Vγ3δ+ T cells (Figure 3D, lower left).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Vγ3δ+ T cells express high levels of ZsGreen.
source: However, closer examination revealed high expression of ZsGreen in these cells (Figure 3B, lower middle).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B (likely Figure 3D based on context).

claim: The Tomato labeling of Vγ3δ+ T cells establishes Fgd5-CreERT2 transgene expression in Vγ3δ+ T cells rather than adult contribution to this lineage.
source: Therefore, rather than establishing adult contribution to this lineage, these experiments established Fgd5-CreERT2 transgene expression in Vγ3δ+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing ZsGreen expression in Vγ3δ+ T cells.

claim: B1a B cells represent an invariant subtype of B cells with a fetal origin that is primarily located in the peritoneum.
source: B1a B cells represent an invariant subtype of B cells with a fetal origin that is primarily located in the peritoneum (Hayakawa et al., 1985), where they co-exists with more traditional B1b and B2 B cells in adult mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Hayakawa et al., 1985.

claim: B1a B cells co-exist with B1b and B2 B cells in the peritoneum of adult mice.
source: B1a B cells represent an invariant subtype of B cells with a fetal origin that is primarily located in the peritoneum (Hayakawa et al., 1985), where they co-exists with more traditional B1b and B2 B cells in adult mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge and citation to Hayakawa et al., 1985.

claim: Less than 10% of B1a B cells display Tomato label in mice with nearly complete HSC labeling.
source: While less than 10% of B1a B cells displayed Tomato label, around 50% of B1b B cells and the vast majority of B2 B cells (Figure 3D right) were Tomato+ (comparable to levels in PB).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Around 50% of B1b B cells display Tomato label in mice with nearly complete HSC labeling.
source: While less than 10% of B1a B cells displayed Tomato label, around 50% of B1b B cells and the vast majority of B2 B cells (Figure 3D right) were Tomato+ (comparable to levels in PB).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The vast majority of B2 B cells display Tomato label in mice with nearly complete HSC labeling.
source: While less than 10% of B1a B cells displayed Tomato label, around 50% of B1b B cells and the vast majority of B2 B cells (Figure 3D right) were Tomato+ (comparable to levels in PB).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The labeling pattern is in line with a more strict fetal/postnatal origin of B1a B cells.
source: This is in line with a more strict fetal/postnatal origin of B1a B cells, the ontogenically mixed origin of B1b B cells (Kantor et al., 1995) and an adult HSC origin of most B2 B cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data and citation to Kantor et al., 1995.

claim: B1b B cells have an ontogenically mixed origin.
source: This is in line with a more strict fetal/postnatal origin of B1a B cells, the ontogenically mixed origin of B1b B cells (Kantor et al., 1995) and an adult HSC origin of most B2 B cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kantor et al., 1995.

claim: Most B2 B cells have an adult HSC origin.
source: This is in line with a more strict fetal/postnatal origin of B1a B cells, the ontogenically mixed origin of B1b B cells (Kantor et al., 1995) and an adult HSC origin of most B2 B cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing high Tomato labeling in B2 B cells.

claim: Microglial cells of the brain have been proposed to arise entirely from embryonic precursor cells.
source: Finally, we investigated adult HSC contribution to microglial cells of the brain, a subset of central nervous system myeloid cells that has been proposed to arise entirely from embryonic precursor cells (Alliot et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Alliot et al., 1999.

claim: IBA-1+ microglia in the brain parenchyma show no detectable Tomato expression in mice with nearly complete HSC labeling.
source: Evaluations by confocal microscopy of the brain parenchyma revealed no detectable Tomato expression in IBA-1+ microglia (Figure 3E), while Fgd5 expressing endothelial cells (Cheng et al., 2012; Gazit et al., 2014) displayed abundant Tomato expression (Figure 3E middle).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Fgd5 expressing endothelial cells display abundant Tomato expression.
source: Evaluations by confocal microscopy of the brain parenchyma revealed no detectable Tomato expression in IBA-1+ microglia (Figure 3E), while Fgd5 expressing endothelial cells (Cheng et al., 2012; Gazit et al., 2014) displayed abundant Tomato expression (Figure 3E middle).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and citations to Cheng et al., 2012 and Gazit et al., 2014.

claim: In aged mice, the initial labeling after 5x Tamoxifen injection is highly specific to HSCs, with only low levels of labeling in MPP2 cells.
source: In aged mice, the initial labeling was highly specific to HSCs, with only low levels of labeling in MPP2 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the aging experiments.

claim: In juvenile mice, a larger fraction of LSKCD150-CD48- MPPs are labeled after 5x Tamoxifen injection compared to aged mice.
source: In sharp contrast, a larger fraction of LSKCD150-CD48- MPPs were labeled in juvenile mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Label progression into all MPP subsets in aged mice is substantially lower when compared to young adult mice.
source: This established that label progression into all MPP subsets in aged mice was substantially lower when compared to young adult mice and further revealed that the HSC contribution to MPPs and MPP3/4s gradually declines with age towards very little replenishment of in particular MPP3/4 in very old age (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The HSC contribution to MPPs and MPP3/4s gradually declines with age towards very little replenishment of MPP3/4 in very old age.
source: This established that label progression into all MPP subsets in aged mice was substantially lower when compared to young adult mice and further revealed that the HSC contribution to MPPs and MPP3/4s gradually declines with age towards very little replenishment of in particular MPP3/4 in very old age (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: No multilineage long-term reconstitution or Tomato+ cells are observed in MPP2/MPP3/4 transplanted mice.
source: As expected, we did not observe any multilineage long-term reconstitution or Tomato+ cells in MPP2/MPP3/4 transplanted mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental transplantation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 10 out of 10 HSC transplanted mice are multi lineage reconstituted at 16 weeks post transplantation with high levels of Tomato+ donor cells in all evaluated lineages.
source: 10 out of 10 HSC transplanted mice were multi lineage reconstituted at 16 weeks post transplantation with high levels of Tomato+ donor cells in all evaluated lineages (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental transplantation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 2 out of 9 MPP transplanted mice display donor reconstitution levels > 1% in all lineages 16 weeks after transplantation.
source: More surprisingly 2 out of 9 MPP transplanted mice displayed donor reconstitution levels > 1% in all lineages 16 weeks after transplantation (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental transplantation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Long-term multilineage reconstitution potential from MPPs is accompanied with robust Tomato labeling among donor cells.
source: This long-term multilineage reconstitution potential from MPPs was accompanied with robust Tomato labeling among donor cells and revealed that Tomato labeled phenotypic MPPs perform as bona fide HSCs after transplantation (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental transplantation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Tomato labeled phenotypic MPPs perform as bona fide HSCs after transplantation.
source: This long-term multilineage reconstitution potential from MPPs was accompanied with robust Tomato labeling among donor cells and revealed that Tomato labeled phenotypic MPPs perform as bona fide HSCs after transplantation (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental transplantation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Mice that received MPP cells and displayed only transient myeloid reconstitution never display any Tomato+ cells.
source: By contrast, mice that received MPP cells and displayed only transient myeloid reconstitution never displayed any Tomato+ cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental transplantation data.

claim: In young mice, there is a minor CD150- HSC activity that appears exclusively coupled to Fgd5 expression.
source: This demonstrates, in young mice, the presence of a minor CD150- HSC activity that appears exclusively coupled to Fgd5 expression.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental transplantation data showing HSC function in Tomato+ MPPs.

claim: The frequency of Tomato labeled HSCs is similar between juvenile (29 days) and aged (87-89 weeks) mice after 1x Tamoxifen labeling.
source: While the frequency of Tomato labeled HSCs was similar among the two groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), all progeny exhibited reduced frequencies of Tomato labeled cells in aged mice, demonstrating a strikingly reduced multilineage differentiation capacity of HSCs as a consequence of age.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: All progeny exhibit reduced frequencies of Tomato labeled cells in aged mice compared to juvenile mice, demonstrating a strikingly reduced multilineage differentiation capacity of HSCs as a consequence of age.
source: While the frequency of Tomato labeled HSCs was similar among the two groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), all progeny exhibited reduced frequencies of Tomato labeled cells in aged mice, demonstrating a strikingly reduced multilineage differentiation capacity of HSCs as a consequence of age.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: HSCs contribute robustly to adult multilineage hematopoiesis in steady state.
source: Our work revealed robust HSC contribution to adult multilineage hematopoiesis
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data from the lineage tracing experiments.

claim: The work supports the previously reported fetal/juvenile origins of several specific hematopoietic subsets.
source: and, while not focused at studying fetal hematopoiesis, support the previously reported fetal/juvenile origins of several other specific hematopoietic subsets.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data showing lack of labeling in certain cell types.

claim: The fastest label progression from HSCs is observed into the platelet lineage.
source: We observed the fastest label progression into the platelet lineage, which might be related to the recent observations that at least a subset of HSCs appears platelet-biased (Sanjuan-Pla et al., 2013; Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the lineage tracing experiments.

claim: At least a subset of HSCs appears platelet-biased.
source: We observed the fastest label progression into the platelet lineage, which might be related to the recent observations that at least a subset of HSCs appears platelet-biased (Sanjuan-Pla et al., 2013; Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sanjuan-Pla et al., 2013 and Shin et al., 2014.

claim: Erythrocytes and granulocytes acquire label with similar kinetics after platelets.
source: Thereafter, erythrocytes and granulocytes acquired label with similar kinetics, although Tomato+ erythrocytes emerged in the peripheral blood somewhat later than granulocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the lineage tracing experiments.

claim: Tomato+ erythrocytes emerge in the peripheral blood somewhat later than granulocytes.
source: Thereafter, erythrocytes and granulocytes acquired label with similar kinetics, although Tomato+ erythrocytes emerged in the peripheral blood somewhat later than granulocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the lineage tracing experiments.

claim: The slower emergence of Tomato+ erythrocytes in peripheral blood compared to granulocytes likely reflects the slower turnover of mature erythrocytes compared to other myeloid cells.
source: This likely reflects the slower turnover of mature erythrocytes compared to other myeloid cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data and knowledge of cell turnover rates.

claim: No noticeable differences are found when evaluating HSC contribution to the neutrophil or eosinophil lineages among granulocytes.
source: On the other hand, among granulocytes, we did not find any noticeable differences when evaluating HSC contribution to the neutrophil or eosinophil lineages (data not shown), despite the seemingly distinct transcriptional underpinnings of these lineages (Drissen et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data (not shown) and citation to Drissen et al., 2016.

claim: Neutrophil and eosinophil lineages have seemingly distinct transcriptional underpinnings.
